newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Long Distance agrees with estimates.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Long Distance agrees with estimates.

text.p: U.S. Long Distance Corp is comfortable with analysts' estimates that it will earn $0.07 per share in the second quarter and $0.30-$0.32 per share in fiscal 1997, President and Chief Executive Officer Larry James said Tuesday.
"We think it's about right," James said of the second quarter estimates. Asked about the year range of $0.30 to $0.32 a share, he said, "We're comfortable with the range."
USLD lost $0.07 per share in the second quarter of 1996. For the year, which ended September 30, 1996, it lost $0.64 per share after special charges, on revenues of $180 million.

In the fast-consolidating long-distance telephone service industry, USLD has been considered a likely takeover target. James, who spoke with Reuters following the company's annual meeting, said there were companies eyeing USLD.
"There's nothing imminent, but there are people who are interested...we've had interest from two or three companies," he said, without naming them.
James said that, at the same time, USLD was considering making an acquisition of its own, buying a company -- again, unnamed -- with revenues of about $40 million a year.
